spec.md was not brought in line with the later rounds: Design still says one plugin file changes (the diff also changes plugin/evals/run.py), and R1 / Acceptance still say 'no runbook record is written' while the test (and plan.md, fix round 2) assert the dispatch's go-requested record stays; plan.md records both departures, the spec does not.

The comment claims that 'a test removed or renamed fails the case too', but pytest exits 5 only when -k selects nothing: removing or renaming one or two of the three named tests still leaves the case green (the lesson's wording, 'when none of them is found', is the accurate one).

The module docstring still says `go` performs the sdlc:go label when 'a person must have applied it', while the change makes it the owner's account only (is_owner_actor); the code's own summary now understates the rule it enforces.

A framework_root case's setup and command checks run in the live framework checkout (--plugin-dir), which later cases load as their plugin, so a case could alter the framework under test for the cases after it; the workspace isolation the other cases get does not apply (doubt: only owner-reviewed cases in the framework's evals/cases reach it, and case 0006 has no setup).

The workflow header a project receives from /sdlc-init still says the job 'checks that a person applied it'; after this change the Go step refuses any account but the owner's, so a project reading its own workflow gets the old rule (the spec kept the file unchanged, and only OPERATING_MODEL.md was updated).
